title: Local lifting of a module presentation of a finite constant quotient
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a finite ring, and $S$ a short exact sequence of sheaves of left $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Suppose $S_3$ is constant [def-constructible-constant] with finitely generated geometric stalks [def-constructible-finite]. There is an etale cover $(U_i\to X)_i$ such that for every $i$ there is a short exact sequence $T_i$ with finitely generated first term $(T_i)_1$ of $\Lambda$-modules, an isomorphism $e_i:\underline{(T_i)_3}\simeq S_3|_{U_i}$, and a map $r_i:\underline{(T_i)_2}\to S_2|_{U_i}$ with $(S.g|_{U_i})\circ r_i=e_i\circ\underline{T_i.g}$. There is no cokernel assertion and no constancy hypothesis on $S_1$.

source.place: Tag 093U, extension paragraph: finite free surjection onto N and simultaneous local lifts of its generators (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/093U)

proof.text: If X is empty, construct the cover with index type PEmpty using Cover.mkOfCovers; the conclusion over its members is vacuous. Otherwise constancy gives N and eN: constant(N) ≅ S.X3. Choose x in X and the geometric point Spec(SeparableClosure κ(x)) -> X. Apply IsFiniteSheaf.isFinitelyGenerated_sheafFiber, transport through sheafFiber.mapIso eN.symm and Point.sheafFiberConstantSheafIso N, and use ModuleCat.isFinitelyGenerated_iff to deduce Module.Finite Lambda N. The Point constant-sheaf API is imported directly, avoiding the cyclic KernelCokernel module.

Apply Module.Finite.exists_fin' to obtain n and a surjective linear map p:(Fin n -> Lambda) -> N. Let T be ShortComplex.moduleCatMk (ker p).subtype p (LinearMap.comp_ker_subtype p). Its exactness follows from ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff: a vector v killed by p is the image of the kernel element (v,hv). Its first map is mono by Subtype.val_injective and its second map is epi by surjectivity of p. The kernel is a finite subset of the finite product Fin n -> Lambda; Module.Finite.of_finite makes T.X1 finitely generated.

Short exactness makes S.g epi. Apply the generic finite-free local lifting theorem to S.g and a = constantSheaf.map T.g followed by eN.hom. This gives one etale cover and a lift r on every member; no constancy assumption on S.X1 is used.

For each member let P be its upperStar functor and c = upperStarConstantSheafIso. Set e = c.symm.app N followed by P.mapIso eN. Rewrite the local lifting equality using Functor.map_comp; c.inv.naturality T.g, composed on the right with P.map eN.hom, gives exactly r followed by P.map S.g = constantSheaf.map T.g followed by e.hom. Return T, its short exactness, finite kernel, e, and r.

proof_origin.place: J3 Lean reduction of Tag 093U: finite stalk model, explicit finite free kernel presentation, generic local free lift, and naturality of the constant-sheaf comparison.
